character.asked: What kind of product is this? (dense-productive / calm-editorial / playful-consumer / premium-restrained)
character.operator_ruling: Playful and inviting, because mathematics is treated as unplayful in conventional thinking. The operator's definition of playful is explicit: mathematics as ART, where art means 'multiple ways to reach the same goal/proof', NOT 'multiple ways to express an emotion'.
character.design_consequence: Playful here means combinatorial and intellectual, not consumer-cute: no candy pastels, no oversized rounded-everything, no bounce for its own sake. Plurality gets made visible: the same event shown as several equivalent paths (calendar/ICS, Meetup, Discord, Mobilizon, the page itself), which is also exactly what the end-state architecture already provides. Energy comes from contrast (size, weight, colour used with intent) rather than from decoration.
character.rejects: the recommended 'calm and editorial' default of round 1

colourFormat.evidence: Tailwind 4 with @theme in src/styles/global.css (no tailwind.config.*, no components.json/shadcn), and the palette the build already resolves to is oklch: blue-600 = oklch(54.6% 0.245 262.881), gray-900 = oklch(21% 0.034 264.665). HSL would mean fighting the framework.

accentAttachment.operator_ruling: "I do like the amber color, because it evokes the idea of golden precision or nobility, which is like the golden ratio and other geometric aspects of mathematics." Alternatives in the same idea-family are invited.
accentAttachment.measured_constraint: One gold cannot do both jobs. The shipped #f59e0b: ink-on-gold = 8.09 PASS, but gold-as-text-on-white = 2.15 FAIL. A deepened gold oklch(55% 0.13 62): gold-as-ink-on-paper = 4.83 PASS, but ink-on-that-gold-surface = 3.27 (large/bold text only). So the system needs two golds: a bright gold floor that dark ink sits on, and a deep gold that is allowed to be text.

paletteProvenance.evidence: Init commit 74c90f6 (2024-11-16, authored 'Alex Berg', package name 'landing-page-book-astro-svelte-tailwind', LICENSE 'Copyright (c) 2020-2030 Alex Berg') already contained src/config.json with theme.color #f59e0b alongside a placeholder domain (mathbookclubsite.com), placeholder email, and boilerplate SEO copy for a generic literary book club; blue-600/blue-100 come from Tailwind 3 defaults used by the template's components (init used tailwindcss ^3.4.4 + @astrojs/tailwind + tailwind.config.cjs). The @theme tokens --color-book-gray/--color-book-theme were introduced by 8ce9607 'style(tailwind): migrate to Tailwind 4 through @tailwindcss/vite' - carried over during migration, not chosen. ec4e0e9 later made ::selection render the declared token instead of a hardcoded #3b82f6, which is why amber paints exactly one surface today.

pathHues.detail: calendar teal oklch(50% 0.11 190) 5.43 / Meetup plum oklch(47% 0.15 305) 7.03 / Discord rose oklch(50% 0.15 25) 6.21 / Mobilizon grass oklch(48% 0.11 150) 5.95 - all AA as text on paper and on their own tints. Rule: a hue appears only where a path exists; tints alone are indistinguishable (1.02) so every chip carries a word and a keyline. Reused for interests (D84). Conditional on the dark ground: >= 40deg separation is required, so chalkboard (152) forces grass to about 105 (set cyan 205 / plum 315 / coral 35 / olive 105, min 47deg) and maroon (27) forces rose to move; sumi (60) and the current set already clear 35deg.
pathHues.final: against chalkboard ink: cyan oklch(50% 0.11 205), plum 47/.15/315, coral 50/.14/35, olive 50/.10/105 - all pass 4.5 as text and >= 40deg from the ink hue

goldRoles.value: gold demoted to accent; and as accent it is a mark, not a surface (round 3b supersedes the bright gold fill)
goldRoles.detail: gold-ink / deep ochre oklch(55% 0.12 62) - text, keylines, hairlines, small marks: 4.81 on paper as text (AA) and 4.81 as a boundary (3.0 bar), and the only gold whose minimum distance to any brand colour tested is 0.135, i.e. brand-neutral. gold-on-dark oklch(76% 0.06 84) - numerals on the dark ground: 6.34 on graphite, 6.80 on sumi, 5.78 on chalkboard, and 0.120 from Amazon orange (twice the distance of any brighter gold). gold-leaf oklch(84% 0.095 86) - the G2 alternative if a bright warm band is wanted: ink on it 10.05, but only 0.073 from Walmart yellow and 0.086 from UMN gold, and invisible as a keyline (1.57). The inherited bright fill oklch(76.9% 0.165 70.1) is withdrawn: 0.019 from Amazon orange, 2.15 as text.
goldRoles.measuredTension: a bright gold fill cannot be made brand-neutral - every L 76-84 value lands 0.07-0.08 from a commerce yellow and 0.086-0.092 from a university gold. Lowering chroma is the only escape: C 0.06 doubles the distance to Amazon orange while keeping AA on dark.
goldRoles.commerceDiagnosis: the commerce read is saturation plus a complementary pair, not gold alone: blue-600 C 0.245 and amber C 0.165 are the only two tokens above a C 0.16 budget, and they sit 167deg apart. Per page today: index.html 6 painted surfaces / 2 chromatic; 404.html and chat/ 1 each.

graphicMotif.value: several paths, one meeting point (derived from the club's own sphere diagram)

typeFamilyConstraintMeasured: PT Serif has no variable build (registry 404), so serif weights are 400+700 only: font-weight 500 and 600 on serif text renders as the regular face and the real bold respectively. A variable sans gives 400/500/600/700 as five distinct renderings from one 26,832 B file.

spacingSizes.value: S3 = 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 px (the 4px grid ratified in round 2, eight named steps)
spacingSizes.evidence: fits 65 of 66 spacing writes (98.5%); the 67th write (-mr-1, a negative margin) is outside the scale. S2 fits 93.9%, powers-of-two 72.7%, a 1.5x rhythm 40.9%.
spacingSizes.open: RESOLVED in ratify 2026-11-01 -> decisions.spacingOrphan (20px illegal: 5 occurrences, 4 live, all -> 24)

fontSizes.operator_ruling: Q3: T3 is fine, as long as you agree the geometry matches the tone we set out in the beginning.

agreement_tested_not_assumed.tone: round 1 set playful = plurality made visible, with energy from contrast of size/weight/colour used with intent, and explicitly no oversized-everything. T3's top step is 3.58x body against T1's 2.99x; the ratio stays 1.200, so the extra step buys contrast without buying a marketing ratio.
agreement_tested_not_assumed.geometry: the display line boxes land on the 4px grid: 33.2->36, 39.8->44, 47.8->52, 57.3->60 px, an arithmetic ladder of step 8. Measured ink of 'Typographic' at 700: 32.7 / 39.8 / 49.0 / 58.2 px, so each grid leading clears by 3.3 / 4.2 / 3.0 / 1.8 px. Tailwind's own pairs collide: 47.8 at 1.00 collides by 1.2 px, 57.3 at 0.98 by 2.0 px.
agreement_tested_not_assumed.guardrail: one display step per screen, mirroring the round-4 rule of one dark band per screen - and the display step is for the WHEN (dates, numerals, the next-meeting line), which is the site's job, not for an invented punchline.
agreement_tested_not_assumed.narrow_cap: at 57.3px the club's own words break the viewport: 'Mathematical' 367.6px and 'Cryptography' 365.1px do not fit 343px (375 viewport), 'Minneapolis' 330.4px does not fit 288px (320 viewport). At 47.8 every word tested fits 343 but not 288. So the top step needs a viewport cap (e.g. 57.3 only above ~700px content, 47.8 below), proved by probe-run.sh rather than by clamp()

corollaries: keylines are inset box-shadows, never borders - a border adds 2px and silently breaks the arithmetic
no control below 24px except a chip, and a chip must then satisfy the WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 spacing exception (probe computes it per axis)

emptyState.value: the zero-upcoming empty state CONVERTS - it is not a sentence and it is never hidden

emptyState.measured: 305px tall in a 375 frame (357px at a 375 viewport) vs 104px for a sentence and 47px for hiding it; built from a 24px status line, an s1 title, a two-line body, a 48px primary (clears the 44px AAA bar) and a 40px secondary, plus the dated line

emptyState.hero: when the snapshot is empty the hero's label changes to 'Nothing scheduled' rather than disappearing, so an empty calendar is distinguishable from a broken page

shadowSemantics.value: hairline = part of the page; shadow = above the page. Two elevation levels, and cards never get one.
shadowSemantics.solved: stop alpha must clear the 1.35 layer bar at the contact edge: black .13 or ink-tinted .165. Adopted stops are INK-TINTED (level 1 .165 at 0 1px 2px; level 2 .22 at 0 2px 5px -1px + .30 at 0 12px 28px -6px), because a black stop wide enough to read at a wide blur paints a 2.10 grey band.
shadowSemantics.shipped: the shipped shadow census in src/ is 17 writes: 1 shadow-sm, 7 shadow-md, 3 shadow-lg, 6 hover:shadow-lg. shadow-md and shadow-lg differ only in offsets - the stop alpha is the same .102 - so both composite to 1.25-1.26 vs paper = FLAT decoration. All 17 come out in design-apply.
shadowSemantics.why_not_three_levels: a card and a hovered card measure the same today; making them distinct puts every card on a visible grey band, which the playful-as-plurality ruling rules out
shadowSemantics.today: nothing in src/ floats (no modal, no dropdown), so both elevation tokens ship unused-but-defined until a menu exists; the linter can forbid box-shadow outside those two tokens CONFIRMED in ratify: both tokens ship defined-but-unused.

noticeAction.value: a notice's action is the `quiet` LABEL with no keyline of its own, at the 40px step, underlined at rest
noticeAction.source: delegate, 2026-11-01, on the operator's blanket ruling: "I'll accept whatever you decide."
noticeAction.rule: a box has exactly ONE boundary: a notice is the only keylined thing in that box
noticeAction.reason_measured: secondary would put a second `rule` hairline 12px inside the notice keyline (3.01 on paper but 2.88 on a panel = illegal), and two identical hairlines at a 12px gap read as a double border; quiet is ground-agnostic (gold 4.82 paper / 4.61 panel, gold-on-ink 5.80 on the band) so the same notice works on all three grounds with zero new tokens
noticeAction.because_gold_is_also_caution: in a caution notice the action is separated from the status word by an underline at rest, its lane and its size - never by a second hue (D102 declines a signal hue)

colourRound9.value: measured, not ratified - the colour round (round 9) is built and measured; the choice of WHERE colour goes, HOW MANY hues, and how the mark's two lines are coloured is the operator's
colourRound9.the_scan: The palette's room is arithmetic, not taste. Round 3b ratified >= 40 degrees of hue separation from the primary and from every reserved path hue. Reserved: ink/rule/tint/band-text at 152, gold/gold-on-ink at 62/84, path hues 35/105/205/315. Put those bands on the wheel and exactly ONE window is left: 246-274 degrees, 29 wide (design/grill/round9-palette.mjs windowScan). So 'add a warm accent' is not available without moving something else.
colourRound9.shipped_breaks_its_own_rule: Measured against the 40-degree bar the shipped palette violates itself twice: gold <-> gold-on-ink 22 degrees (fine - per-ground twins of one role), but gold <-> path-discord 27 degrees and path-mobilizon <-> gold-on-ink 21 degrees. Whether that is an exception to write down or a bug to fix is open.
colourRound9.arithmetic_that_decides_token_shape: For any colour between paper and ink in luminance, contrast-on-paper x contrast-on-ink = the paper-ink pair (12.02). Asking 4.5 text on paper AND 3.0 graphics on ink asks 4.5 x 3.0 = 13.5 > 12.02, so it is impossible with one value. This is the proof behind every -on-ink twin and behind MARK_COLOURS being keyed per ground; it is not a style preference.
colourRound9.measured: node design/round9.mjs (design/grill/round9/report.json). Panels are cropped from the specimen and counted pixel by pixel at the check:color bar (chroma >= 0.04) and at a second bar (>= 0.08) that sits above every neutral in @theme, plus the 0.01-0.04 'faint' band: S-A (as shipped) 13.6% chromatic / 0.0% at >= 0.08 / 2 hue families; S-B (colour where it means something) 12.7% / 0.4% / 5 families; S-C (colour as area, tinted fields) 12.9% / 0.5% / 6 families but 46.9% faint. Palette rows: H-A 2.0%/0.3%/3 families, H-B (accent from the open window) 1.8%/0%/2, H-C (re-arranged warm) 2.1%/0.3%/2.
colourRound9.key_finding: The shipped tints are not colour to a measurement or to an eye: oklch(95% 0.03 ...) sits at chroma 0.03, under the census bar, so a tinted field reads as 'faint' (S-C: 46.9% of pixels faint, 0.5% at the level a reader would call colour). Buying area with the existing tints therefore does nothing measurable; area needs chroma above ~0.04 or a darker field.
colourRound9.fails: One planted pair fails on painted bytes: gold on a tinted hero field = 4.39 against the 4.5 text bar (gold on paper is 4.82). Colour put on a tint loses contrast it has on paper. Everything else clears: path words on ink 4.74/4.59/4.91, chips on path tints 10.67-10.94, accent 4.56 on paper and 4.5 on ink, warm olive 5.22 on paper / 5.08 on ink.
colourRound9.candidates_measured: H-B accent, the best brand-separated point in the only open window: hue 266, L 55.5, C 0.06 - 4.61 predicted, 4.56 painted on paper, on-ink twin 4.5. Both clear by under 0.1, i.e. inside the noise of a font change, and its nearest commerce brand is 0.11 (Walmart blue) against gold's D88 bar of 0.135 - so it is less brand-clean than the gold it would sit beside. H-C warm set (w-gold 55/0.12/50, w-olive 52/0.1/100 and their on-ink twins) only becomes legal under re-arrangement R-4 (fold the gold twins into one family, retire path-mobilizon, move discord), and R-4 costs 12 measured pairs to re-solve and re-measure. Retiring mobilizon alone (R-1), or moving gold+discord (R-2/R-3), does NOT open a warm window - measured.
colourRound9.mark: Four colourings (K-A as shipped, K-B one route line gold, K-C one route line accent, K-D both route lines gold) measure essentially the same painted coverage: paper 8.10-8.15% of box, px at/over the 1.5 device-px floor 3930-3973 of 4508-4536 ink pixels, share at 3.0 bars 60.5-62.6%. So colouring the two lines costs nothing in stroke survival; the choice is about whether two lines stay TWO things, which is measured by luminance separation and the 0.05 same-colour bar, not by coverage.
colourRound9.tooling: design/grill/okcolor.mjs is now the shared OKLab/OKLCH/contrast/hue-window/brand-distance module (its --selftest asserts paper-ink 12.02, gold 4.82, D88 0.135, the 0.05 same-colour bar); design/color-survey.mjs and the round 9 modules all import it, so the predictor and the survey cannot drift. Contrast pairs are measured off bytes the browser paints (colour read back through a 1px canvas, render-measure.js's method) and re-computed from the @theme token it names; the two agreeing is the check.
colourRound9.trap_this_exists_to_prevent: A specimen that CLAIMS a surface it does not paint. Three planted pairs in the first round-9 specimen named `ink on tint` or `ink on ink` on elements sitting on paper or inheriting band-text, and measured contrast 1.00 - which reads as a palette failure and is a specimen bug. design/round9.mjs now compares each SIDE (declared token bytes vs painted bytes, delta-OKLab >= 0.05) and exits 1, so a mislabel cannot silently become a ruling.
colourRound9.open: RULED IN PART 2026-11-02. Approved: H-A (no new hue; spend colour on area and on things that mean something). Accepted provisionally: K-B (one route line gold, gold-on-ink on dark grounds) 'until we find something better' — hold the caveat that all four mark colourings measure the same coverage, so K-B buys distinctness of the two lines, not legibility. Chosen: PH-B (colour where it means something + real photographs), which lands in the round-10 slot specimen rather than in the palette. STILL OPEN: surface policy S-A/S-B/S-C; whether the shipped gold <-> path-discord 27° (and path-mobilizon <-> gold-on-ink 21°) is a recorded exception or a defect to fix; and whether the leading/body line-spacing misses ride this round or take their own.

round9Rulings.value: operator rulings 2026-11-02 on grill round 9: H-A approved, K-B accepted provisionally, PH-B chosen over PH-A
round9Rulings.h_a: No new hue. The measured reasons: the only open window (246-274) yields an accent at 4.56 on paper and 4.5 on ink — both clearing by under 0.1, i.e. inside the noise of a font change — and its nearest commerce brand sits at 0.11, worse than gold's ratified 0.135 floor (D88). A warm accent is legal only after the R-4 re-arrangement, which costs 12 measured pairs to re-solve and re-measure. So the free win is area and meaning, not a new token.
round9Rulings.k_b: One route line in gold (gold-on-ink on dark grounds). Coverage is flat across K-A..K-D (ink share 8.10-8.15% of box; 3930-3973 px at the 1.5 device-px floor of 4508-4536; 60.5-62.6% of its ink at the 3.0 bar), and the 4.82 gold pair is already painted by the shipped mark's accents — so the ruling buys a visible difference between the two lines (12.02 vs 4.82 separates in greyscale; 4.82 vs 4.59 does not) and costs no geometry. Re-measure with design/mark-pixels.mjs before the mark shrinks further.
round9Rulings.ph_b: Colour where it means something AND real photographs, with the places reserved now so the shot list has sizes and an empty state has a defined look. Sizes in .notes/asset-sources.md; drawn to scale in design/grill/round-10-photos.html.
round9Rulings.not_a_ruling: S-A/S-B/S-C was NOT answered — the operator's 'Q1' was a new question about whitespace, not the surface policy. Ask it again; S-B remains the recommendation (2 to 5 hue families, reader-visible share 0.0% to 0.4%, every pair clears).

areaAndWhitespace.value: measured, not ratified — 'mostly whitespace' is an area problem with four different remedies, and the page is thin rather than wide
areaAndWhitespace.instrument: design/whitespace-survey.mjs (npm run check:space), records in .design/tmp-whitespace/. Two bars, named: painted = delta-OKLab >= 0.05 against each pixel's own ground (the same bar okcolor.mjs uses in token space); emptiness = rows in the block-flow walk with no painted pixel at all.
areaAndWhitespace.measured: 1240: document 2495px tall (2607px after the lazy image decodes — a 112px reflow), painted 5.48%, empty runs >= 60px = 8 runs totalling 41.5% of height, biggest 303px. 390: 4078px tall, painted 8.23%, 32.5% empty, biggest 320px. Surfaces at 1240: header 1240x64 paints 4.8% and carries 64 chars; hero 372x564 paints 43.6%, 468 chars; panel section 1240x633, 866 chars; main's trailing block 372x564 paints 8.8%, 263 chars; footer 1240x131 paints 0.8%, 131 chars. Media: hero mark 372x233 (2.75%), Meetup png 200x192 (1.24%), icons 24x24. Structure: declared padding 256px + inter-surface margins 480px.
areaAndWhitespace.the_finding: Every text surface is already inside WCAG's 80-100 characters per line and npm run lines reports no failure, so the emptiness is not line length: it is thin content per surface, structural gaps, and the absence of media. The panel section's 866 characters are six generic boilerplate cards, so 'more copy' would worsen the site while improving the number.
areaAndWhitespace.levers_ranked_by_measured_area: PS-1 hero photo 372x564 = 6.78% of the page; PS-2 venue strip 1228x320 = 12.70% (1228 is the document's own content width, measured); PS-3 join cell 200x192 -> 420x268; PS-4 event thumb 367x120 inside the 367x205 card. Then the two disabled event sections (config.json showUpcomingEvents/showPastEvents = false; the dates do not live in this repo, roadmap-events.md, and D69 forbids making Meetup's feed an architecture input). Then vertical rhythm: 480px of margin/padding at 1240. Colour is the smallest lever: S-B moves the reader-visible share 0.0% -> 0.4%.
areaAndWhitespace.side_finding: The site rule is 'a hairline rule at most', and what breaks it today is mass rather than weight: the header band is 1240x64 with 4.8% of its pixels differing from the page behind it (a solid full-bleed band, 60px of it empty above a 32px row) and the footer 1240x131 at 0.8%. A rule that spans nothing and a band that spans everything are the same mistake at different opacities.
areaAndWhitespace.tooling: design/round10.mjs builds the slot specimen from the survey JSON and then measures the DRAWING back in Firefox, exiting 1 if any box is > 1px off the number printed in its own data-w/data-h (it caught a missing box-sizing on first run). okcolor.mjs gained oklabBytes()/distLab() plus a selftest assertion that the pixel-space distance equals the token-space distance at both the 0.5 and 0.25 bars, so the survey's pixel bar and the token drift bar cannot be two different measurements.

thirdPartyMarks.value: ruled 2026-11-02 — a third party's mark is never our brand colour; platforms are named in our type, and any mark shown is the official file, unmodified, labelled
thirdPartyMarks.why_measured_first: The round-9 census found exactly two hue families on the landing page: ours (150-180deg, 3.234%) and Meetup's red (0-30deg, 0.523%, mean chroma 0.226 — the highest in the system). The png paints 1.24% of the desktop page. So the site's strongest colour belongs to another company, and removing it costs 0.52 points of chromatic share (3.77% -> ~3.25%). The operator's two instructions (less drab, fewer foreign marks) pull opposite ways; area and true content have to pay.
thirdPartyMarks.retrieved: Discord's brand page (curl + Firefox UA, 2026-11-02): the marks are 'the exclusive property of Discord Inc'; 'You must have permission from Discord before using any of the Discord Marks or Brand Assets except as permitted here'; use may not 'imply that you are Discord, or somehow sponsored by or acting on behalf of Discord'; the don'ts include editing, distorting or recolouring the logo. Meetup's are NOT retrievable from this rig: /brand is a JS shell, /terms/ and help.meetup.com return 403, only /license-attribution/index.html is a real document and it is about their use of third-party licences. Recorded as UNVERIFIED, not as absent.
thirdPartyMarks.doctrine: Nominative use (9th Circuit, summarised from a tertiary source, not primary): the thing cannot readily be identified without the mark; only as much of the mark as that requires — the worked example is 'the words but not the font or symbol'; and nothing suggests sponsorship. A link to the club's own Meetup page is factor-1 use; a 200x192 png is more than identification requires.
thirdPartyMarks.applied: 1) name platforms in our own words + a link; the path-* hues stay ours (path-meetup oklch(47% 0.15 315) vs the png's rgb(237 28 64)). 2) if a mark appears it is the official file, unmodified, in clearspace, next to the name — a recoloured third-party mark is the risk their terms name. 3) one static footer line, specific wording, no TrademarkNotice component (a component invites conditional logic that will be wrong; the line costs ~16px of a 131px footer). 4) keep the account links — demoting a mark is not demoting the funnel.
thirdPartyMarks.also_found: The png's markup says width=200 height=80 while the file is 834x799, and preflight sets img { height: auto }, so the rendered box is 200x192; lazy-loaded, it reflowed the document 2495 -> 2607px (112px) when it decoded. Every photo slot therefore carries a declared aspect ratio.
thirdPartyMarks.queue: Drop or shrink the png in src/components/JoinCommunity.astro and add the footer attribution line. Not a colour edit — its cost is stated above.
